children: Apple

is reportedly pulling back from two ambitious MacBook concepts, scrapping plans for both a large foldable laptop and a separate mid-sized OLED model as the company reshapes its Mac product roadmap. The cancellations could signal greater caution around expensive display technologies, but Apple's broader transition toward OLED MacBooks remains intact.
According to research firm Omdia, Apple abandoned development of a
16.1-inch to 18-inch foldable MacBook
and another OLED MacBook expected to measure between
14.4 and 16.1 inches
. Apple has not confirmed either project or their reported cancellation.
The shift leaves the roughly
14.3-inch to 16.3-inch range
centered on Apple's MacBook Pro lineup.
But Apple is not retreating from OLED altogether. Omdia expects
14.3-inch and 16.3-inch OLED MacBook Pro models
to arrive as early as late 2026 or early 2027, while existing mini-LED versions could remain available through at least 2028.
Apple is also reportedly exploring a new
13.8-inch OLED MacBook for 2029
, potentially creating another tier between the MacBook Air and MacBook Pro. That machine could include integrated touch sensing, an under-display camera and newer OLED technology.
The product reshuffle comes as the Mac business is showing renewed momentum. Apple generated
$10.4 billion in Mac revenue in fiscal Q3, up 29% year over year
, setting a June-quarter record. Total company revenue reached
$109.4 billion, up 16%
What Apple investors should watch next
The reported cancellations matter less as lost near-term revenue opportunities than as clues about Apple's hardware strategy.
Investors should watch the timing and pricing of the first OLED MacBook Pros, manufacturing yields and whether Apple ultimately creates another MacBook tier below the Pro.

If Apple can bring OLED into Macs without materially raising costs or cannibalizing existing models, the display transition could support another premium upgrade cycle. The bigger risk is that increasingly complex hardware designs become too expensive to manufacture at Apple's required scale.

title: Apple Makes Surprising Shift in Future MacBook Lineup
